correctness.rationale: A metric-preserving partial injection of rank>=3 either stays in leaf-to-leaf symmetric inverse monoid or fixes hub; a hub-fixed map cannot be nilpotent. At rank2, hub crossings are directed i->0->j paths with i!=j, while hub 2-cycles are excluded; rank1 adds 2m single hub-leaf arrows. The remaining nilpotent leaf partial injections are exactly disjoint oriented directed paths, including isolated vertices. A j-chain contributes x^j u^{j-1} to a labeled EGF, so E_l=exp(sum_{j<=l}x^j u^{j-1}) and E_l-E_{l-1} extracts maximum chain size l (nilpotency index). This proves the exact joint polynomial and m![x^m]exp(x/(1-x))+m(m+1) total. Independently enumerated every partial injection on m+1 vertices and checked star metric/nilpotent powers for m=1..5, totals (3,9,25,93,531); the full original rank/index script was also read, but bounded counts do not prove m arbitrary. The Gumbel limit follows from independent Poisson chain counts with means rho_m^j conditioned on total size m, where rho/(1-rho)^2=m and rho=1-m^-1/2+O(m^-1). At L=floor(sqrt(m)(0.5logm+s)), tail Poisson mean rho^(L+1)/(1-rho)->e^-s; a Fourier lattice local CLT for total size has scale m^3/4 and truncated-tail mean/variance o(scale/scale^2), giving conditioning ratio1. The source provides the Fourier small/large arc estimates; the hub correction m(m+1) is negligible compared with at least m! leaf chains. The proof asserts weak convergence only, not a finite error bound.
residual_risks: The local CLT is an analytic step based on Fourier inversion, not established by finite m<=5 enumeration.
